A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CASAL research, with matchable main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices. Some response examples overflow page boundaries, but their underlying text is recoverable and the substantive comparison remains reliable.

before.justification: v1 reports original hallucination-reduction experiments, capability evaluations, OOD transfer, multimodal and MoE results, and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds GRPO comparisons, Landmark-VQA results and a comparative activation analysis.

M1.justification: CASAL retains knowledge probing, difference-in-means steering targets, local representation-loss training and weight substitution. Algorithm 1 clarifies initialization and the returned model. Last-token extraction, activation caching and weight reinsertion were already described in v1 Appendices C–D; these are not new method components.

E1.justification: Table 5 adds Landmark-VQA, extending visual QA from food identification to landmark/place identification. WorldCuisines, the three text QA datasets and the general-capability benchmarks remain. This is a limited domain extension within the existing multimodal evaluation.

E2.justification: GRPO gains reported comparisons in Tables 1–5. Tables 3–5 additionally introduce SFT and DPO into OOD and WorldCuisines experiments that previously compared only the original model with CASAL. CAA remains in Appendix E. Despite its revised caption, Figure 2 does not actually add a GRPO curve.

E3.justification: The new Appendix Q analysis compares PCA projections at layers 16, 17 and 18 across the baseline, SFT, DPO, GRPO and CASAL. Existing probing settings, metrics, model sizes and listed training hyperparameters remain unchanged. Detailed GRPO and Landmark-VQA protocols are not supplied.

E4.justification: Appendix Q/Figure 22 adds a comparative analysis of whether different training methods separate known and unknown activations. Appendix O adds a second food-image response example. Existing CAA comparisons, probing-threshold tests, submodule ablations and hyperparameter sensitivity analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions use the same plus/minus reporting practice without adding run counts, seeds, uncertainty definitions or statistical-testing procedures. Revised uncertainty values in existing tables and additional rows using this practice are result changes, not changes in statistical reporting methodology.

E6.justification: New comparator results across Tables 1–5 substantially extend the empirical evidence. Landmark-VQA reports hallucination rates of 75.78%±1.69 for the baseline and 31.25%±8.32 for CASAL. Table 4 revises CASAL's TriviaQA training value from 28.83%±1.53 to 18.23%±1.03, while its EntityQA test value remains 11.72%±1.66. Some uncertainty values in Tables 2–3 also change.

T1.justification: The steering and loss equations, amortized-optimization discussion in Appendix B, FLOPs derivations in Appendix N and MoE mathematics in Appendix P are retained. Algorithm notation and diagrams are clarified, without adding or substantively revising formal definitions, assumptions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the principal effectiveness, efficiency and generality claims. Section 3.1 extends the sample-efficiency comparison to GRPO. The conclusion modestly qualifies the broader scalability claim, changing 'demonstrates' a general principle to 'provides initial evidence' for it.

C2.justification: The introduction shifts its explanation of hallucinations from RLHF helpfulness incentives toward training and evaluation rewarding guessing. Section 3.2 adds explanations of efficiency scaling with model depth and answer length; Section 3.3 interprets the new comparative PCA evidence. The stated reasoning-model and long-generation limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Existing implementation information, hyperparameters, hardware, training-time estimates and dataset/model access links are retained. The main-text clarifications about cached activations and weight substitution were already documented in v1's appendices. Appendix M adds GRPO to its heading but supplies no corresponding training details; Landmark-VQA also lacks detailed documentation.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning relative to activation steering, representation learning and amortized optimization remain the same. Expanded author lists, URLs, bibliographic metadata and citation suffix changes do not introduce new research references or materially revise the novelty positioning.

P1.justification: v2 revises several introductory and methodological paragraphs, expands the compute-efficiency explanation, clarifies Algorithm 1 and adds acknowledgements. Author affiliations and bibliography formatting are updated. The main narrative structure and most appendix prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures 1 and 4–6 are redrawn, comparison tables are expanded, and Table 5 becomes an illustrated two-dataset display. New appendix image examples and the multi-panel Figure 22 substantially extend the visual presentation. Some inconsistencies remain: Figure 2's caption mentions an absent GRPO curve, and Figure 22 labels both color classes 'Unknown'.

improvement.justification: v2 improves the empirical assessment by adding trained comparators to previously baseline-only OOD and WorldCuisines evaluations, alongside Landmark-VQA and comparative activation evidence. Clearer explanations also help readers understand the existing method. The gain is limited by missing GRPO and Landmark-VQA setup details, the unsupported GRPO extension in Figure 2's caption, and Figure 22's ambiguous legend. These additions provide useful context without establishing a substantial overall quality improvement.
